cells.tense: You are starting this with a clear head, right here, with the pen in your hand.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Take the direction that's here, cut past the noise to the single reason it matters, and act on that reason the same day.
cells.core:
You are shutting and clearing with the fire already lit, and it is not an accident. You can tell which things have ended and what the next move is, and you act on it while knowing the ending is still going. What you had going has a visible finish, and you are not pretending otherwise. That is why the new thing does not have to wait for the room to be empty. You can start on ground that is still being swept.

The head clears first, and the body follows it. Cut to the reason this matters and act on that reason the same day. The ending is not a delay to sit in; it is the cleared space your fire is already using. Keep it moving and the clearing closes behind you.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is clear and the fire is lit.
cells.verb: starting the fire before knowing where it will lead
cells.place: in the clearing, where what was ends

cells.tense: You are braced at the ending, clearing rooms that haven't emptied yet.
cells.act: perceive it with fresh eyes before judging
cells.ask: Sit with something that's actually finishing and look at it again before you decide what it was.
cells.core:
Here is how this looks when it works: the ground gets cleared, a fire starts on it, and both happen in one motion. You name what ended, you start the next thing, and nothing waits on permission. The spark and the ending share a week.

Yours runs the other way. The plans get made before the present can hold them, rooms are being cleared that haven't emptied, and the thing genuinely finishing goes unperceived because you're already living in the cleared version. Sit with something that's finishing and look at it again before you decide what it was. What you see may not match the forecast, and that is the point.
cells.sheetLine: You are clearing a room that isn't empty yet.
cells.verb: starting the fire before knowing where it will lead
cells.place: in the clearing, where what was ends

cells.tense: The endings finished and nothing here is lighting the way forward.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Take something young into your hands and keep it going — water it, shift it toward light, notice what it asks for.
cells.core:
A version of this exists where the ending and the fire land together: ground clears, something starts on it, the whole thing in one motion and no waiting on permission.

That version isn't where you are. The door shut behind you and nothing here is lighting up. The fire that would move you is quiet, and you are not in the middle of beginning anything. Take something young into your hands and keep it going — water it, shift it toward light, notice what it asks for. It won't restart your spark by will, and it doesn't need to. It keeps your hands working with something alive until the beginning finds you again.

cells.tense: You are starting things and calling it just paying attention, without the pen.
cells.ask: Give the thing you began in this clearing one weekday hour, held as something you mean.
cells.core:
The authored version goes like this: you start the fire, you know you started it, and it burns because you tended it from cleared ground. Nobody handed it to you.

All of that is already true of what you have going. You've been starting things through endings — a direction, a pull, a next thing — and your own name for it is that you are just paying attention. The clearing is real; the fire is also real. It shows through your hands while the version you tell leaves it out. Give the thing you began in this clearing one weekday hour, held as something you mean. Clearings belong to your life, and so does what you start in them.
cells.sheetLine: You are starting something and calling it paying attention.
cells.verb: starting the fire before knowing where it will lead
cells.place: in the clearing, where what was ends
